interfaces.name: User erasure fan-out
interfaces.contract:
Flow:
1. DELETE /api/v1/users/me (api_auth.py, WS-08) requires header X-Reauth-Token (IF-17) and calls UserService.delete_user(user_id, reason) -> UUID erasure_request_id.
2. Local erasure runs through UserDataErasure (idempotent, retry-safe); the users row is soft-deleted and anonymized last.
3. In the same transaction as the erasure_requests row (slot 012), UserDeletedKafkaEvent(user_id, reason, metadata.correlation_id = erasure_request_id) is published on solace.users through publish(conn=).
4. Each PHI service's group solace-group-erasure-<service> runs its UserDataErasure under acting_as_user(user_id), purges in-process caches, writes ACCOUNT_ERASED_IN_SERVICE (IF-14) and publishes user.erasure.completed; ErasureIncomplete becomes RetryableEventError.
5. user-service records completions per service; erasure is complete when every expected service has reported; GET /api/v1/admin/erasure-requests/{request_id} (ADMIN) shows per-service status.

Helper src/solace_infrastructure/gdpr/consumer.py: def register_user_erasure_consumer(plane: ServiceEventPlane, *, service_name: str, erasure: UserDataErasure, purge_caches: Callable[[UUID], Awaitable[None]] | None = None) -> None.

Expected services and stores: orchestrator (threads, checkpoints via delete_threads), safety (assessments, history; escalations pseudonymized), therapy, diagnosis, memory (Postgres, Redis, Weaviate when enabled, BM25), personality (with tombstone), notification (delivery records erased, crisis episodes pseudonymized), event tables via erase_user_events (WS-06). Audit rows hold no PHI and are retained (D-24).

interfaces.name: Identity, session and MFA API
interfaces.contract:
Access-token claims: sub, type='access', roles, sid (session id), amr (['pwd'] | ['pwd','otp'] | ['google'] | ['google','otp']), mfa: bool, cns (IF-08), iss 'solace-ai', aud 'solace-ai-api', iat, exp (15 min). Refresh tokens carry sid and jti (30 days). Refresh requires the sid to be active; rotation is atomic (Redis Lua swap) with a 30 s grace for an exact replay of the same jti; reuse after the grace revokes the session; token type is checked before the blacklist; status and role are re-read; session activity is extended. Logout or password change revokes the sid and its refresh tokens in the shared blacklist.

Endpoints (prefix /api/v1/auth, api_auth.py):
- POST /register: always 202-shaped, no email-exists oracle (an existing owner gets an email).
- POST /login: tokens, or {mfa_required: true, mfa_token} (5 min) when MFA is enrolled, or {mfa_enrollment_required: true, enrollment_token} for a CLINICIAN/ADMIN without a factor.
- POST /mfa/verify {mfa_token, code | recovery_code}; POST /mfa/enroll/start -> {otpauth_uri, secret} shown once; POST /mfa/enroll/confirm {code} -> {recovery_codes: [10]} shown once. TOTP is RFC 6238 (30 s, 6 digits, +-1 step) and rejects replay of the last used step.
- POST /password/forgot {email}: always 202. POST /password/reset {token, new_password}: 30 min, single use, hashed at rest; revokes all sessions.
- POST /reauth {password | code} -> {reauth_token} (5 min, type='reauth').
- POST /verify-email {token}: expiring, hashed token; strict envs refuse login for unverified accounts.
- GET /oauth/google/start?redirect_uri=<allow-listed in OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_ORIGINS> sets an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax state cookie; GET /oauth/google/callback validates state against the cookie, links only by the verified Google sub in oauth_accounts (an existing password account with the same email links only after proving its password) and 302-redirects with a one-time 60 s code; POST /oauth/google/exchange {code} -> token pair. Google endpoints come from GOOGLE_OAUTH_* so the stub IdP can stand in.

Account routes in api_auth.py: POST /api/v1/users/me/password (current password verified before hashing, throttled); DELETE /api/v1/users/me (requires X-Reauth-Token).

CLINICIAN and ADMIN tokens without mfa=true get 403 on PHI, admin and acknowledgement endpoints via require_mfa_for_roles (IF-04, W4). JWKS at GET /.well-known/jwks.json once RS256 is on.

interfaces.name: Observability: health, metrics and alerts
interfaces.contract:
Every service exposes /live, /ready, /health (= /ready) and /metrics on its own port (IF-01). Docker HEALTHCHECK, compose depends_on health conditions, autoheal and Caddy active health checks use /live, never /ready, so a dependency outage never cuts users off from in-band crisis resources; /ready drives readiness tests and alerts.

Standard metrics (prometheus_client; labels never hold user ids or text): solace_http_requests_total{service,route,method,status}, solace_http_request_duration_seconds{service,route}, solace_readiness_check_ok{service,check}, solace_background_task_up{service,task}, solace_crisis_detected_total{source,level}, solace_llm_fallback_total{service,reason}, solace_audit_write_failures_total{service}, solace_audit_chain_verify_ok, solace_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds{store}, plus the IF-05 and IF-09 metrics.

Prometheus scrapes <compose-service>:<port>/metrics for the 9 MVP services. Rules in infrastructure/prometheus/rules/solace.yml, promtool-tested:
- W1: CrisisAlertDeliveryFailed (any failed outcome in 5 m), CrisisOutboxBacklog (oldest pending > 120 s), NotificationConsumerLag (> 10 for 5 m), DLQUnresolved (> 0), CrisisAlertsUnacknowledged (> 0 for 20 m), CrisisEventPublishFailures (> 0), ServiceNotReady (2 m).
- W4: ContainerUnhealthy, HostDiskUsage (> 80%), BackupStale (> 26 h), AuditWriteFailures (> 0), AuditChainVerifyFailed.
Alertmanager (docker-compose.observability.yml) routes to ALERTMANAGER_EMAIL_TO through the SMTP relay (mailpit in test). Autoheal restarts unhealthy containers (W4).

interfaces.name: Real-infra and E2E harness
interfaces.contract:
Markers (registered by WS-01): realinfra, e2e, contract, clinical. SOLACE_REQUIRE_REALINFRA=1 turns skips into failures at barriers.

src/solace_testing/realinfra.py session fixtures (testcontainers):
- pg_migrated -> PgHandle(dsn_app, dsn_migrator, dsn_superuser, app_pool): postgres:16 pinned, migrated to head by scripts.db.migrate as solace_migrator, accessed as solace_app with RLS;
- redis_url: redis:7 with a password;
- kafka_bootstrap: cp-kafka 7.5 with aiokafka helpers produce(topic, event) and consume_until(topic, predicate, timeout);
- smtp_sink -> SmtpSink(api_url).wait_for(to, subject_contains, timeout=60) on mailpit;
- fake_llm -> base_url.
Component tests live in tests/realinfra/<ws-slug>/.

tests/e2e/conftest.py:
- e2e_stack (session) -> Stack(urls: dict[service, base_url], edge_url, project, mailpit_api, fake_llm_control, pg_superuser_dsn), built with 'docker compose -p solace-e2e-<lane> -f docker-compose.yml [-f docker-compose.prod.yml] -f docker-compose.test.yml' on Docker-assigned 127.0.0.1 ports; client traffic goes through the edge Caddy so TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1 is exercised.
- Helpers: make_user(stack, role='user', verified=True) -> TestUser{id, email, password, access_token} (register, then the mailpit verification link); provision_clinician(stack, email, phone, on_call=True, backup=False) via scripts.provision_clinician; fault.stop/start/restart/pause(service); read_logs(service); kafka_lag(group) via the broker CLI in the kafka container; llm.scenario(mode, match=None) and llm.requests(); oidc stub (W3).
- Env: SOLACE_E2E_PROFILE in {dev, strict}; SOLACE_E2E_ENVIRONMENT in {staging, production}; SOLACE_E2E_KEEP=1 keeps the stack.

docker-compose.test.yml adds fake-llm, mailpit (axllent/mailpit pinned by digest) and a stub OIDC provider; generates per-run test secrets; sets EMAIL_SMTP_HOST=mailpit, EMAIL_SMTP_TLS_MODE=none, LLM_PORTKEY_GATEWAY_URL=http://fake-llm:8080/v1, LLM_PHI_EGRESS_APPROVED=true (stub only), NOTIFICATION_FALLBACK_ONCALL_EMAIL=fallback-oncall@test.invalid, http-only CADDY_*_SITE values and ephemeral loopback ports. It never weakens strict settings otherwise.

Manifest tests/e2e/expected_failures.yaml lists {test_id, expected_failing_hop, target_wave}; the plugin applies strict xfail and fails the barrier when a listed test passes early or fails at a different hop.

interfaces.name: Contract-test framework
interfaces.contract:
solace_testing.contracts:
- Contract files are JSON under tests/contracts/<consumer>__<provider>/<interaction>.json: {consumer, provider, interaction, request: {method, path, headers_required: [...], body_example}, response: {status, body_schema (JSON Schema)}}.
- verify_provider(app: FastAPI, contracts_dir: Path, *, auth_headers: Callable[[str], dict]) runs in the provider's suite against the real app through httpx ASGITransport.
- assert_request_matches(contract, request) runs in consumer suites.
- Event contracts {event_type, example} are validated against solace_events.schemas.EVENT_REGISTRY for every producer/consumer pair (CrisisDetectedEvent, EscalationTriggeredEvent, SafetyAssessmentEvent, UserDeletedKafkaEvent, UserErasureCompletedKafkaEvent).
- The consumer workstream writes the contract file; the provider workstream makes verify_provider pass. Marker contract.

interfaces.name: Build, image and test tooling
interfaces.contract:
Dependencies: requirements.in (direct runtime deps) compiled by 'uv pip compile --generate-hashes --python-version 3.12' into requirements.lock; requirements-dev.in into requirements-dev.lock (pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-timeout, hypothesis, testcontainers[postgres,redis,kafka], aiokafka, websockets); services/<svc>/requirements.txt hold service extras only.

Images: build context is the repo root; FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:<pinned>; 'uv pip sync requirements.lock' into /opt/venv with no fallback; non-root uid 1000; WORKDIR /app; PYTHONPATH=/app:/app/src.
- Each image's CMD imports the same module path its test suite imports. Underscore services run 'python -m uvicorn services.<pkg>.src.main:app'; user-service and notification-service merge their src into /app/src and run 'src.main:app' (notification's package-relative imports require it); analytics-service keeps its current top-level layout unless its owner moves it.
- ENTRYPOINT ['/app/docker/entrypoint.sh']: for every NAME_FILE variable it exports NAME from the file (one trailing newline stripped; a missing file is fatal), then exec "$@".
- uvicorn runs with --no-access-log --proxy-headers; HEALTHCHECK probes /live.
- docker/migrate.Dockerfile builds solace-migrate carrying migrations/, alembic.ini and scripts/db.

Import roots: shared packages are imported only as top-level solace_* (never src.solace_*), enforced by tests/build/test_import_roots.py; src/solace_infrastructure/__init__.py and infrastructure/api_gateway/__init__.py export lazily.

Makefile targets: lint (ruff E9,F63,F7,F82), test-unit (one pytest process per suite), test-realinfra, test-e2e PROFILE=dev|strict, test-clinical, test-contract, images, clean-checkout TREE=<tree id> (build from a git archive), ci-local (all of the above). .github/workflows/ci.yml mirrors them.

interfaces.name: Secrets and key-material contract
interfaces.contract:
Every strict-environment secret comes from the per-environment secrets store (D-07): AWS Secrets Manager names solace/<env>/<NAME>, fetched at deploy time by deploy/render_secrets.py (host instance role) into a root-owned tmpfs at /run/secrets/<name> and referenced by NAME_FILE, which docker/entrypoint.sh loads.

Secret names: AUTH_SECRET_KEY, AUTH_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM, SERVICE_TOKEN_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM (one per service, W4), ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY, ENCRYPTION_SEARCH_HASH_SALT, ENCRYPTION_RETIRED_KEYS_JSON, AUDIT_HMAC_KEY, FERNET_TOKEN_KEY, FERNET_FIELD_KEY, POSTGRES_PASSWORD (solace_app), POSTGRES_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD, REDIS_PASSWORD, REDIS_URL, WEAVIATE_API_KEY, LLM_PORTKEY_API_KEY, LLM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, EMAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD, SMS_AUTH_TOKEN, GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD, BASIC_AUTH_HASH, BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, and the Postgres TLS files postgres-ca.crt, server.crt, server.key.

Rules:
- Each container receives only the secrets its service reads; Caddy receives only DOMAIN, CADDY_ADMIN_EMAIL and BASIC_AUTH_HASH.
- Dev and test values are generated per developer or per run by deploy/env/generate_dev_env.py (writes files with restrictive ACLs, prints names only, refuses to overwrite without --rotate); ProductionGuards rejects known dev values and low-entropy values in strict envs.
- Key material (ENCRYPTION_*, AUDIT_HMAC_KEY, AUTH_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM, SERVICE_TOKEN_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM, BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY) is versioned in the store with deletion protection and escrow; backups record key ids, never keys.
- No secret is ever in the repo, an image layer, a compose literal, a log line, a test report or tool output.

decisions.question: What is the schema of record: the Alembic chain or the column names the repositories were written against?
decisions.recommended_default: Alembic (001 to head plus slots 009-021) is the only schema of record, and repository SQL changes to match it. 001 and 007 are repaired in place in W0 because no database has ever applied them. No service runs DDL at runtime: outbox, DLQ, audit and LangGraph checkpoint DDL move into slots, and the dead orchestrator_checkpoints DDL in state.py is deleted.
decisions.rationale: Migrations are the only artifact that can be versioned, reviewed and applied by a migrate job, and they already carry the RLS, width and constraint decisions. Repository SQL disagrees with them in five services (MVP-034/060/061/080/096/128/220), so one side must yield, and Alembic is the reviewable side.
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: Which database topology and roles should the pilot use?
decisions.recommended_default: One PostgreSQL 16 container with one database 'solace' (schema public). solace_migrator owns all tables and is used only by the migrate job; solace_app (NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, DML only) is used by every service from Wave 0; the image superuser 'postgres' is ops-only (init, physical backup and restore, test assertions). The nine unused per-service databases in init-db are dropped; per-service roles are post-MVP.
decisions.rationale: Superuser connections bypass every RLS policy (MVP-041). Moving to the real role in W0 means every later persistence task is proven under RLS instead of being flipped late, and physical backups avoid the pg_dump-versus-FORCE-RLS conflict.
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: Which inter-service authentication model should services use?
decisions.recommended_default: Short-lived service JWTs from ServiceTokenManager, carrying metadata.obo_sub for user-scoped calls; the shared get_current_user accepts them only from services granted service:act_for_user (orchestrator only); a service handling an obo call forwards the inbound header for same-user downstream calls; service-only endpoints enforce require_service_permission with receiver-side permission resolution; user JWTs are never forwarded or stored in graph state. HS256 with AUTH_SECRET_KEY for service tokens in W1-W3; from W4, per-service RS256 service keys (kid = service name) and RS256-only user tokens.
decisions.rationale: Today no single credential works across services (MVP-021). Forwarding user JWTs would put credentials into checkpointed LangGraph state and break on 15-minute expiry in long WS sessions. obo tokens leave receivers' ownership checks unchanged, and per-service keys stop a compromised container from minting another service's identity.
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: Which LLM and embedding vendors may receive real-user PHI, which BAAs are in place, and are Portkey semantic caching and memory's OpenAI embeddings acceptable?
decisions.recommended_default: Portkey gateway to Anthropic only after BAAs covering both are confirmed (Anthropic via AWS Bedrock under the AWS BAA is the alternative). LLM_ENABLE_CACHING=false for every request and never a semantic cache for PHI prompts. memory-service's direct OpenAI embedding calls disabled and Weaviate writes off (WEAVIATE_ENABLED=false); retrieval stays keyword/BM25. Prompts limited to minimum-necessary content. In strict envs LLM_PHI_EGRESS_APPROVED=true is required to enable a real provider; without BAAs by the release gate the pilot runs template replies only. Tests always use the fake LLM.
decisions.rationale: PHI currently flows to a cache shared across users (MVP-056) and to OpenAI directly (MVP-145). Both are legal exposures that code alone cannot fix, and the crisis path must already work with the LLM unavailable.
decisions.answer: Anthropic models on AWS Bedrock under the AWS BAA are the only route for real-user PHI. Strict environments require LLM_PROVIDER=bedrock; Portkey stays for development and test with synthetic data only. LLM features stay off for real users until the AWS BAA is accepted in AWS Artifact and recorded. Caching off, no semantic cache, memory's OpenAI embeddings disabled and Weaviate writes off, as in the default. Adds one W1 task in WS-09 (Bedrock provider).

decisions.question: Clinical sign-off: who approves the crisis lexicon, the CRITICAL threshold, the LLM/fallback fusion rule, negation policy and auto-escalation rules?
decisions.recommended_default: Ship lexicon v1 in solace_clinical, built from safety's clinical_lexicon.json plus every register gap (suicidal, ending my life, jump off, took all my pills, homicidal, abuse, curly apostrophes), with a positive/negative phrase set of 200 or more. CRITICAL floor 0.85. Max-only fusion: LLM, fallback and stub scores may raise, never lower, a lexicon level and are never averaged in. No HIGH on context-free single words without self-reference. W1 proceeds on this default with the owner's acceptance recorded as a ledger Ruling; a named licensed clinician signs docs/CLINICAL-VALIDATION.md before W5 (required for W5 scoring changes and the release gate).
decisions.rationale: Detection is the top patient-safety risk (MVP-017, 023-026, 030, 084, 086, 182). Engineering can make detection conservative now, but clinical accountability needs a named approver and one reviewed artifact used by every detector.
decisions.answer: Build on the default now; a named clinician signs off before go-live.

decisions.question: Crisis-mode semantics: does crisis state persist per thread, how does it clear, and how are repeated alerts deduplicated?
decisions.recommended_default: Safety flags are per turn. After HIGH/CRITICAL the thread enters a 'crisis watch' for the next 3 user turns or 30 minutes: resources appended, the safety-service check mandatory, the ELEVATED threshold lowered; no permanent lock. Pages coalesce per user into one episode for 15 minutes unless the level rises; after acknowledgement, further detections in the window send one update to the acknowledging clinician. ELEVATED shows resources and pages no one; RISK_ALERT monitoring emails are coalesced per user per window.
decisions.rationale: Today's OR-merge reducer locks a thread into the crisis reply forever after one false positive and re-pages every turn (MVP-019, 181, 299). A bounded watch keeps the protective intent without that failure.
decisions.answer: Build on the default now; a named clinician signs off before go-live.

decisions.question: Which secrets manager holds per-environment secrets?
decisions.recommended_default: AWS Secrets Manager, one secret set per environment with separate KMS keys, rendered at deploy time by deploy/render_secrets.py into root-only tmpfs /run/secrets files consumed through NAME_FILE. For a non-AWS host: SOPS-encrypted per-environment files with age keys held off-host. The plaintext .env.prod and Caddy's env_file are retired, and the keys in the working-tree .env are rotated.
decisions.rationale: Every secret is hand-generated into one plaintext file injected into all 11 containers, Caddy included (MVP-348/349). Per-environment separation, least exposure and rotation need a store.
decisions.answer: SOPS + age instead of AWS Secrets Manager: per-environment encrypted deploy/secrets/<env>.sops.yaml, one age key pair per environment with the private keys held off-host, decrypted at deploy by deploy/render_secrets.py into root-only tmpfs /run/secrets (NAME_FILE contract unchanged). The plaintext .env.prod and Caddy env_file are retired and the working-tree .env keys rotated.

decisions.question: Which MFA method, and who must use it?
decisions.recommended_default: TOTP (RFC 6238, 30 s, 6 digits, +-1 step) with 10 one-time recovery codes; mandatory for CLINICIAN and ADMIN (enrollment forced at first login; no PHI, admin or acknowledgement API without mfa=true); optional for end users; TOTP secrets encrypted with the PHI codec. The one-time acknowledgement link in alert emails stays usable without login. WebAuthn and SMS OTP are post-MVP.
decisions.rationale: Clinicians and admins reach PHI across users and are password-only today (MVP-344). TOTP needs no new vendor or BAA, and pyotp is already available; the amr/mfa claims are designed in W2 so W4 is additive.
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: Which backup tooling and RPO/RTO targets apply?
decisions.recommended_default: Postgres: wal-g (or pgBackRest) physical base backup nightly plus continuous WAL archiving to an encrypted off-host target (S3 with SSE-KMS, versioning and a 35-day object lock on AWS; an encrypted external volume on a local host); RPO 15 min, RTO 4 h. Redis and Kafka are not backed up (ephemeral by design; the Postgres outbox is the durable event source). Weaviate is not backed up while writes are off (D-04). Keys are escrowed in the secrets store. An automated restore drill runs in W4, before release and then monthly. Fallback if wal-g is too heavy: 6-hourly physical snapshots (RPO 6 h).
decisions.rationale: No backup exists for any PHI store and all data sits on one deletable volume (MVP-037/043/350). A backup counts only once a restore has been tested, and physical backups avoid the FORCE RLS restriction on pg_dump.
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default. RPO 15 min, RTO 4 h.

decisions.question: Where is the audit trail stored, and how long is it retained?
decisions.recommended_default: Postgres audit_events in the same database (slot 011); solace_app has INSERT and SELECT only with append-only rules; one global HMAC chain serialized by advisory lock; AUDIT_HMAC_KEY in the secrets store; rows hold ids and action codes only, so they survive erasure; retained 6 years and included in backups; a nightly verify_chain job alerts on mismatch.
decisions.rationale: The audit logger is never called (MVP-091), the chain cannot detect tampering (MVP-345) and per-process tips fork it (MVP-346). One serialized, backed-up store that recomputes HMACs fixes all three.
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: Client contract: does the code or docs/API-HANDOFF.md define the REST/WS protocol and the OAuth handoff?
decisions.recommended_default: The code becomes the contract and API-HANDOFF is rewritten from it (IF-12). WS frames use the documented names (chat.message/content in; safety.alert, chat.response, pong, error out) and accept the legacy {type:'message', message} as an alias; unknown frames get an error frame instead of a silent drop. Errors on the edge services (orchestrator, user-service) use {error:{code,message,request_id}} from W2; internal services keep FastAPI's {detail} shape. OAuth returns by 302 with a one-time code exchanged by POST. The pilot client targets this API, not Supabase.
decisions.rationale: Clients built from the doc today have their frames dropped silently (MVP-072) and OAuth cannot hand tokens to a client (MVP-104). No client exists yet, so adopting the documented names costs nothing and the crisis E2E in W1 needs the final frames.
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: Which notification providers deliver clinician alerts, and what may an alert contain?
decisions.recommended_default: Email through an SMTP relay covered by a BAA (e.g. Amazon SES in the pilot region) with STARTTLS (EMAIL_SMTP_TLS_MODE=starttls); SMS through Twilio with a BAA as an optional second channel for CRITICAL; push out of scope. Alerts carry level, categories, detection sources, time, alert id and the acknowledgement link, plus the user's display name and contact only when the user gave crisis-contact consent (D-23); never message text or diagnosis. The fallback mailbox is a monitored shared clinical inbox on a different provider.
decisions.rationale: Alerts cannot reach anyone today (MVP-011/064), an alert without the user's identity is not actionable, and the provider and content rules decide what PHI leaves the system.
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default. Amazon SES email.

decisions.question: How are clinician and admin accounts provisioned and placed on call?
decisions.recommended_default: Only an operator creates them, with scripts/provision_clinician.py run in the user-service container: a verified ACTIVE account with an E.164 phone, on-call/backup flags and a one-time set-password link. ADMIN toggles on-call status and assignments through the admin endpoints (IF-08). No self-registration for privileged roles. Before go-live at least two on-call clinicians and the fallback mailbox are configured. MFA becomes mandatory once W4 lands.
decisions.rationale: No supported path creates a clinician or stores a phone number, so the on-call roster is empty (MVP-105).
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default. At least two on-call clinicians (primary and backup) plus a fallback mailbox; names are an owner action before go-live.

decisions.question: Which ENVIRONMENT value does the pilot run with, and is staging strict?
decisions.recommended_default: The pilot runs ENVIRONMENT=production; a staging rehearsal uses ENVIRONMENT=staging with identical strictness; every guard keyed on 'production' only switches to is_strict_environment().
decisions.rationale: The documented deploy runs staging, which silently skips the production-only guards: in-memory outbox, DLQ, escalations and the verification gate (MVP-028/052/088/213).
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: Should the bundled Postgres use TLS on the single host?
decisions.recommended_default: Yes: TLS on, with a CA and server certificate generated at deploy time (scripts/db/gen_certs.py) and stored in the secrets store; clients use POSTGRES_SSL_MODE=verify-full against host 'postgres' with POSTGRES_SSL_ROOT_CERT; the dev profile may use 'prefer'.
decisions.rationale: Strict envs already force sslmode=require, which the TLS-less bundled Postgres rejects (MVP-010), and 'require' skips certificate verification (MVP-271). verify-full satisfies the guards and protects PHI in transit.
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default. TLS with verify-full.

decisions.question: What is the dependency baseline?
decisions.recommended_default: One uv lock for Python 3.12 pinned to the versions the 5,377 local tests pass on (langgraph 1.0.4, langgraph-checkpoint 3.0.1, langchain-core 1.2.28, pydantic 2.13.x, pydantic-settings 2.12.0, fastapi 0.128.0, asyncpg 0.30.0, redis 5.3.x, weaviate-client 4.19.x), plus security bumps (PyJWT >= 2.13, python-jose removed) and the missing packages (email-validator, aiokafka, langgraph-checkpoint-postgres with psycopg, pyotp). No torch, transformers or VADER in images (lexicon-only safety). Base images pinned by digest.
decisions.rationale: Images would ship langgraph 0.2.x with a checkpoint CVE while tests run on 1.x (MVP-358); PyJWT pins sit in 2026 advisory ranges (MVP-359); the current pins cannot resolve (MVP-005).
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: Commit policy: when does the owner commit the interdependent working tree?
decisions.recommended_default: The owner commits the whole working tree, untracked files included, as one unit at the W0 barrier and at each later barrier. Until then, clean-checkout consistency is proven by building images from a git archive of the checkpoint tree.
decisions.rationale: HEAD does not work without the uncommitted tree (MVP-008), and checkpoint trees are the only safety net against an accidental clean.
decisions.answer: No commits at all during the program, by agents or the owner. The working tree and commit-free checkpoint trees are the record; clean-checkout checks build from git archive of a checkpoint tree; each barrier tree is also exported as a zip outside the repo. The owner decides about committing after the program.

decisions.question: Is analytics-service part of the pilot?
decisions.recommended_default: Keep it as a non-critical, staff-only operator dashboard: fix ingestion, PHI logging and role checks; no clinical workflow depends on it; ClickHouse stays out of scope and counters hold no PHI.
decisions.rationale: Its issues are in scope and its outputs help monitor the pilot, but it must not hold up the critical path.
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default. Analytics stays as a staff-only dashboard.

decisions.question: What happens to out-of-scope components that are deployed or imported today?
decisions.recommended_default: config-service is removed from the MVP compose, prod overlay and CI image matrix and its code frozen; feature flags stay in solace_infrastructure.feature_flags. The Kong package stays unimported behind a lazy __init__. ClickHouse, the memory RAG pipeline and the safety contraindication engine stay unwired, and code or docs that claim they run are corrected.
decisions.rationale: config-service has zero consumers and is permanently unhealthy (MVP-231); eager imports of dead packages break boot (MVP-269, 310); dead engines mislead reviewers (MVP-174).
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: May pinned packages be installed into the local Python 3.12 environment?
decisions.recommended_default: Yes, once at W0 entry: install exactly the lock versions of the packages the suites need but the anaconda env lacks or has at vulnerable versions (aiokafka, langgraph-checkpoint-postgres, PyJWT upgraded to >= 2.13, plus any other lock-pinned test extra), recording 'pip freeze' before and after. Later additions need owner approval. Fallback if refused: Kafka-client and checkpointer tests run inside a test-runner container built from requirements-dev.lock.
decisions.rationale: aiokafka and langgraph-checkpoint-postgres are not installed, and real-infra event-plane and checkpointer tests need them; installing packages is a stop condition in the execution protocol.
decisions.answer: A dedicated venv at D:\tmp\mvp-exec\venv instead of installing into anaconda. Created at W0 entry from the anaconda 3.12.3 interpreter with --system-site-packages (anaconda is read, never modified); the missing pins (aiokafka, langgraph-checkpoint-postgres with psycopg, PyJWT >= 2.13) go into the venv only, with pip freeze before and after; per-suite baseline re-recorded. After WS-01's lock lands the venv is re-synced to it, and the W0 barrier also runs the suites in a clean venv built only from the lock.

decisions.question: How is clinician access to patient data scoped?
decisions.recommended_default: A clinician reads or writes a user's PHI only when assigned to that user (clinician_patient_assignments) or when acknowledging an open crisis episode for that user within 72 h. Admins have no PHI read endpoints. Cross-user DB work sets the RLS user to the data owner only after can_access_subject passes. No BYPASSRLS role for services.
decisions.rationale: Any clinician can reach every user's data today (MVP-120), and the RLS context uses the caller instead of the data owner (MVP-141).
decisions.answer: Build on the default now; a named clinician signs off before go-live.

decisions.question: What is the ingress screening architecture and its fail-safe?
decisions.recommended_default: The local shared-lexicon screen runs first on every message; the safety-service /check runs on every message with a 2 s timeout and can only raise the level (fuse_risk); if /check fails or times out the local result stands and the turn is marked degraded; the LLM intent classifier always runs for non-crisis messages when available and an LLM crisis_disclosure routes to the crisis path; in-band resources never depend on the LLM, downstream services, Kafka or the database.
decisions.rationale: The safety-service precheck is never enabled (MVP-017), LLM classification is skipped or never routed (MVP-023/024), and a graph exception drops crisis resources (MVP-079).
decisions.answer: Build on the default now; a named clinician signs off before go-live.

decisions.question: Which consents are required, and how is revocation enforced?
decisions.recommended_default: Terms of service, privacy notice, and an AI-companion plus crisis-handling disclosure (versioned) must be accepted before the first chat; crisis-contact consent (a clinician may contact the user in a crisis, and the alert may carry their name and contact) is requested at signup and recorded separately. All are stored in consent_records with the document version. Access tokens carry the 'cns' claim and the orchestrator returns 403 CONSENT_REQUIRED without it; revoking a required consent ends sessions and blocks chat without deleting the account. Research and marketing consents are optional.
decisions.rationale: Consent is recorded but never enforced (MVP-100), and contacting a user in crisis needs a documented basis.
decisions.answer: Build the default; legal reviews before go-live.

decisions.question: What erasure SLA and retention apply to PHI, audit rows, event payloads, crisis records and backups?
decisions.recommended_default: Deletion is immediate and irreversible after re-authentication and confirmation. PHI is hard-deleted everywhere within 15 minutes (target) and at most 24 h: rows, checkpoints, Redis, Weaviate, caches, and outbox/DLQ rows for the user. Crisis episodes and escalation records are pseudonymized (user reference replaced by a salted hash, contact data removed) rather than deleted, for duty-of-care documentation. Audit rows (no PHI) and consent records are kept for the legal retention period. Outbox and DLQ payloads are purged 7 and 30 days after publish or resolution; Kafka solace.safety and solace.users retain 7 days; backups age out within 35 days, documented as the erasure lag.
decisions.rationale: Erasure never fans out (MVP-029), event tables keep plaintext PHI forever (MVP-054), and crisis-response records may need to outlive the account; retention needs a legal basis.
decisions.answer: Build the default; legal reviews before go-live.

decisions.question: Where does the release gate run, and which host runs the pilot?
decisions.recommended_default: The release gate runs on a local Docker host with the strict production profile. AWS staging is provisioned only after the owner grants the deployer IAM policy. Go-live needs the AWS host (or an owner-approved alternative) with D-09 off-host backups.
decisions.rationale: AWS provisioning is blocked on IAM permissions and the CFN template has never been deployed (MVP-043).
decisions.answer: AWS (account 253025918446, us-east-1) hosts the release gate and the pilot, using the existing IAM user MedCodex-Local for now. The 2026-10-19 IAM simulation shows only Bedrock allowed; CloudFormation, EC2, SSM, S3, KMS and SES are denied, so the deployer policy must be attached to MedCodex-Local before W4's off-host backups, W5's release gate and go-live. Until then real-infra tests run on local Docker; an unattached policy at W5 entry is a stop.

decisions.question: Edge rate limiting: a custom Caddy build or app-level limits only, and what happens when the limiter backend fails?
decisions.recommended_default: The app-level Redis limiter (IF-04), keyed on user id or the real client IP with TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1, is the control. On Redis failure it fails closed (503) for auth routes and open for chat, with a metric and alert. Caddy gets request-size and timeout limits but no third-party module, and the misleading rate-limit comment is removed.
decisions.rationale: Stock Caddy has no rate_limit module (MVP-115), proxy-IP keying lets about 21 bad logins a minute lock out everyone (MVP-101), and a Redis outage currently returns 500 on every login (MVP-185).
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: How does a WebSocket carry the token, and how does re-authentication work?
decisions.recommended_default: Prefer the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol pair ('solace.v1', 'bearer.<jwt>'); keep '?token=' for compatibility with uvicorn and Caddy access logs disabled; check exp and revocation on every frame; accept {type:'auth', token} re-auth frames; close with 4401 on expiry, revocation or account deletion.
decisions.rationale: The WS validates the token only at the handshake (MVP-163) and query tokens land in logs (MVP-211).
decisions.answer: Accepted as the default.

decisions.question: Should there be one clinician-alert path, and which component is the alert system of record?
decisions.recommended_default: notification-service is the only component that pages clinicians and the system of record for crisis episodes (coalescing, acknowledgement, re-paging). safety-service records its escalation decisions durably and publishes them only through its transactional outbox; it stops calling /notifications/send inline. The orchestrator, safety, diagnosis and therapy publish CrisisDetected with the turn correlation id, and notification coalesces them into one episode.
decisions.rationale: Inline escalation can never deliver, blocks /check for up to 300 s (MVP-085/087) and triples pages (MVP-181/299); acknowledgement belongs where pages are sent, and keeping it there avoids a race between the first page and the escalation record (MVP-082).
decisions.answer: Build on the default now; a named clinician signs off before go-live.

decisions.question: Which crisis resources are shown, and for which locale?
decisions.recommended_default: US pilot (en-US): 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988), Crisis Text Line (text HOME to 741741), 911 for immediate danger. Versioned in solace_clinical and returned identically by the orchestrator and safety-service. Non-US users are outside the pilot.
decisions.rationale: Resources are hard-coded in several places today; a single versioned source is needed for clinical sign-off.
decisions.answer: Several countries, US first: crisis resources become a per-locale versioned registry with only en-US populated (988, 741741, 911); the user's locale reaches the screen without a DB or network call; an unsupported locale gets a safe generic fallback. Each further country is added with clinician-verified resources before its users join. Resources still need the clinician's sign-off.

decisions.question: May diagnostic hypotheses or labels appear in user-facing replies during the pilot?
decisions.recommended_default: No. Diagnosis contributes symptom and risk signals to the orchestrator only; therapy never asserts a diagnosis the user did not state (no default 'Depression' plan); personality style adaptation is allowed.
decisions.rationale: The product is screening-grade, not a diagnostic device, and diagnosis and therapy outputs are clinically unreliable today (MVP-048, 125, 202).
decisions.answer: Build on the default now; a named clinician signs off before go-live.

decisions.question: What is the go-live gate for real users and real PHI?
decisions.recommended_default: Only synthetic data until the W5 release gate passes and, in addition, the D-04 BAAs, the D-05 clinical sign-off, D-13 on-call coverage and D-09 restore-drill evidence are recorded. The first real users are a named pilot cohort.
decisions.rationale: Every PHI and crisis control was nominal until this program; real users must not arrive before those controls are proven.
decisions.answer: Build the default; legal reviews before go-live.

global_constraints: Python 3.12 only. Local interpreter: the program venv D:\tmp\mvp-exec\venv\Scripts\python.exe (D-20), created at W0 entry from the anaconda 3.12.3 interpreter with --system-site-packages and called by full path from the PowerShell tool (the bare 'python' shim and the Bash tool hook are broken). Nothing is ever installed into anaconda. Images use python:3.12-slim pinned by digest from W0. No runtime or test dependency is added except through WS-01's lock.

Unit tests use exactly this PowerShell command, one pytest process per suite: $env:PYTHONPATH="D:\Repo\Contextual-Chatbot;D:\Repo\Contextual-Chatbot\src"; $env:ENVIRONMENT="test"; & D:\tmp\mvp-exec\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest <suite> -o "addopts=" -p no:logging -q. Suites: each tests/<dir> (solace_events, solace_security, solace_infrastructure, solace_common, solace_testing, integration, alignment, security, migrations, scripts, system, config_service, plus the new bootstrap, build, deploy, contracts, clinical), tests/test_syntax_and_imports.py, infrastructure/api_gateway/tests and each services/<svc>/tests. Baseline 5,377 passed in anaconda, re-recorded per suite in the venv at W0 entry; counts are compared at every barrier and a drop needs a ledger Ruling.

Real-infra tests carry marker realinfra (testcontainers, tests/realinfra/<ws-slug>/) or e2e (compose stack, tests/e2e/, project solace-e2e-<lane>, Docker-assigned 127.0.0.1 ports). At most 2 lanes run them at once; stacks are torn down with their volumes. At barriers SOLACE_REQUIRE_REALINFRA=1 is set, so a skipped realinfra or e2e test fails.

No git commit, branch, worktree, stash, reset, checkout, clean or push, and the real git index is never touched. Every task starts and ends with D:\tmp\mvp-exec\tools\checkpoint.ps1 -Label "<task>:base" / "<task>:head"; review packages come from review-package.ps1; rollback only via rollback.ps1. Nobody commits during the program, the owner included (D-17); each barrier tree is also exported with git archive to a zip outside the repo.

Implementers edit only their task's declared files, all inside their workstream's owned_paths; contended files follow the shared_files protocols. Work needed in another workstream's files is a supporting task in that workstream's lane citing the issue id; the issue-owning workstream writes the acceptance test and closes the issue only when every part has landed. New test files are named test_mvp_<id>_<slug>.py; an existing test file is edited only by the owner of the code under test.

TDD in six steps per task: write the failing test; run it and record RED for the defect's reason; write the minimal fix; run to GREEN; run the owning suite; checkpoint. A defect test that passes before the fix is a finding against the task. Test names or docstrings cite the MVP id they prove.

Strict environments are ENVIRONMENT in {staging, production} (solace_infrastructure.runtime.is_strict_environment); the pilot runs production. In strict envs a missing or failing declared dependency (secret, Postgres, Redis, Kafka/event plane, codec, audit store, peer URL, LLM configuration when egress is approved) fails startup; no in-memory store or localhost default stands in for PHI, crisis events, sessions, tokens, rate limits, the outbox or the DLQ. Development/test fallbacks log WARNING and make /ready 503. No guard is keyed on 'production' alone.

Lifespans contain no try/except that swallows a platform-component failure. /ready reflects real dependency state; Docker healthchecks and Caddy use /live; a degraded agent result is never reported as success.

Schema changes go only through the Alembic slot files (IF-03), as phase-A tasks run one at a time in a per-wave schema lane. Services connect as solace_app and run no DDL. RLS policies use NULLIF(current_setting('app.current_user_id', true), '')::uuid; RLS tables are accessed only through ConnectionPoolManager.acquire()/transaction(); work without a request runs inside acting_as_user(user_id).

PHI rules: never log, emit, cache, return in errors, or put into metric labels any message text, symptoms, diagnoses, names, emails, phone numbers, tokens or secrets. Events carry ids and category codes only. PHI columns go through solace_security.phi_codec with the owner as AAD. No PHI goes to a third party except via Anthropic models on AWS Bedrock under the AWS BAA (D-04) with caching off, or in clinician alerts under D-12. Tests use synthetic data only. Never print .env or generated secret values in tool output, reports or tests.
Client-visible errors never include str(exception), SQL or stack traces; bodies follow {error:{code,message,request_id}} per IF-01.

Crisis invariants: in-band resources never depend on the LLM, downstream services, Kafka or the database; fusion is max-only and no change may lower a lexicon-derived level; every HIGH/CRITICAL detection writes a durable outbox row before the response returns, or counts and alerts a publish failure; pages are coalesced per IF-09; changes to the lexicon, thresholds or escalation behaviour need the D-05/D-06 record and must keep tests/clinical green.

Inter-service calls use IF-04 tokens only (obo for user-scoped calls, forwarded inbound headers for same-user downstream calls); user JWTs are never forwarded and no credential enters LangGraph state. Every hop propagates X-Request-ID, X-Correlation-ID and X-Turn-ID, has an explicit timeout, and retries a POST only with an Idempotency-Key the provider honours.

Environment variable names follow IF-02; a new setting is requested as an env-registry entry from WS-03 in the same wave and enforced by tests/deploy/test_env_contract.py. /metrics, /docs, /openapi.json, /status and /api/v1/internal/* are never routed by Caddy.

Latency budgets: crisis screen < 5 ms per message; safety-service check 2 s (on timeout the local result stands and 'degraded' reports it); per-hop agent timeout 8 s; turn deadline 20 s; crisis resources in the response within 3 s in E2E; crisis alert delivery within 60 s in E2E.

Models and reviews: Sonnet 5.5 implements well-specified standard tasks. Every safety-critical or security-critical task gets an Opus 5.5 implementer, an Opus 5.5 reviewer and an AGY adversarial review; design-heavy tasks (IF-01, IF-04, IF-05, IF-07, IF-09, IF-13, IF-14, IF-16, the harness) are Opus 5.5. Fix rounds 1-3 resume the implementer; rounds 4-5 use a fresh Opus 5.5. Implementers never spawn subagents. AGY runs only through the gemini plugin MCP with engine agy, on an exported snapshot, never on the real repo.

Each wave runs phase A first: platform lanes touching src/**, services/shared/**, migrations/**, infrastructure/**, the seven event_bridge.py files, compose, CI, build or requirements (this includes service-owned slot files, src/solace_clinical and src/solace_infrastructure/gdpr). Phase B (service lanes) follows. At most 6 implementers run concurrently; full regression runs only at barriers.
An interface is frozen at the start of the wave that first uses it. Any change needs a ledger Ruling naming every consumer workstream, and the consumers' tests are updated in the same wave.

Tests never call real LLM, SMTP, SMS or OAuth providers; only the fake LLM, mailpit and the stub OIDC provider. Installing packages beyond D-20 or anywhere except the program venv, pulling unpinned images, provisioning cloud resources, pushing, or touching anything outside the working tree and D:\tmp\mvp-exec requires owner approval (stop condition).

Out of scope, do not edit: services/config_service/** beyond removing it from compose; Kong modules beyond import decoupling; ClickHouse paths; the RBAC/ABAC policy engine; HA/DR, horizontal scaling and load/chaos work. Post-MVP ids MVP-333 to MVP-343 are not scheduled.

When a task completes, its Status in docs/mvp/TRACKER.md is set to done (python docs/mvp/tools/mvp_docs.py set ...); register statuses are derived from the tracker (an entry is fixed when every task covering it is done). docs/MVP-ISSUE-REGISTER.md is re-rendered by the controller at each wave barrier and is not owned by any workstream; docs/mvp/** is controller-only and excluded from scope-breach checks.
review_focus: Crisis disclosures outside the signed-off phrase set, which become ingress false negatives on the deployed configuration: misspellings, slang and leetspeak, non-English or code-switched text, emoji, quoted or hypothetical speech, risk that builds across several turns, and long messages where a negation in an earlier clause precedes the disclosure.

Concurrent and partial failures on the alert path that lose, duplicate or strand clinician pages: a crash between the domain write and the outbox row or between delivery and idempotency recording, a consumer rebalance mid-batch, SMTP accepting then bouncing, two pollers or reapers after a restart, and an acknowledgement racing a re-page.

Foreign-but-valid identifiers and context-less work under the real solace_app/RLS role: another user's thread_id, session_id, plan_id or alert id, a clinician without an assignment, consumers and CLIs running without acting_as_user that silently read or write nothing, and an RLS user left set on a pooled connection.

PHI escaping through unplanned sinks: exception text in logs or error bodies, nested or non-string structlog values, outbox/DLQ/Kafka payloads, LLM prompts and cache keys, uvicorn or Caddy access logs (including WS query tokens), metric labels, checkpoint rows and alert emails.

Strict-environment boots with partially valid configuration, and long-lived drift, that degrade silently while tests that set env explicitly stay green: one secret missing or malformed, a Redis password not propagated, a renamed variable restoring a dev default, tokens expiring mid-WebSocket, key rotation with old ciphertext, and a restore onto a newer schema.
test_strategy:
Four tiers, each with a fixed home and marker.

1. Unit and in-process: the existing 5,377 tests plus a RED-first test for every defect, run with the global command in one pytest process per suite; mocks only at process boundaries. The clinical phrase set (tests/clinical, marker clinical) and hypothesis tests of normalize_text/screen_text run in every barrier regression against every detector.

2. Contract (marker contract, IF-20, tests/contracts): for every orchestrator-to-service call, therapy-to-memory, the client REST/WS protocol and every event producer/consumer pair, the consumer's contract file is verified against the provider's real FastAPI app and pydantic schemas in-process, catching URL, credential, field-name, enum-case and status drift without containers. Event contracts start in W1, REST contracts in W2.

3. Real-infra component (marker realinfra, tests/realinfra/<ws-slug>/, IF-19 fixtures on testcontainers): postgres:16 migrated by the real scripts.db.migrate as solace_migrator and accessed as solace_app under RLS; redis:7 with a password; cp-kafka 7.5 through aiokafka; mailpit; the fake LLM. Every workstream uses it for repository-vs-schema round trips with ciphertext checked in raw SQL, RLS denial, event-plane crash/redelivery/poison/reaper/idempotency semantics, per-store erasure, refresh-token rotation and audit-chain concurrency. tests/migrations/test_chain_real_pg.py runs upgrade head, downgrade base, upgrade head on every slot change.

4. E2E acceptance (marker e2e, tests/e2e, WS-05): the real images through docker-compose.yml + docker-compose.test.yml (dev) or + docker-compose.prod.yml (strict, ENVIRONMENT=production or staging) with per-run generated secrets, fake LLM, mailpit and a stub OIDC provider, on Docker-assigned 127.0.0.1 ports, with client traffic through the edge Caddy so proxy-hop logic is exercised. Tests use only public endpoints, create users through the real register and verification flow and clinicians through the provisioning CLI, and assert side effects on real infrastructure (mailpit messages and their lack of PHI, episode and escalation rows read as the image superuser, ciphertext at rest, zero foreign rows under solace_app, Alertmanager emails), never just HTTP status. Progress is tracked in tests/e2e/expected_failures.yaml as strict xfail with the expected failing hop; a listed test that passes early or fails at a different hop blocks the barrier.

Wave proof: each wave's acceptance suites are written in phase A from the frozen interfaces and must fail for the documented reason before phase B. W0: boot/migrate smoke in dev and strict, plus the crisis E2E red at documented hops in dev. W1: crisis delivery over REST and WS in both profiles, fault injection (graph exception, notification outage, SMTP rejection, Kafka down at boot, LLM failure, safety-service down, duplicate detections, unacknowledged re-page) and the negative-phrase E2E, plus crisis-path alerts reaching mailpit. W2: chat journey, restart durability, encryption at rest, contract suite, identity sessions. W3: deletion completeness across every store, isolation matrix, audit tamper detection and concurrency, PHI capture scan, secrets injection, consent gate, OAuth against the stub IdP. W4: MFA, password reset, restore drill with measured RPO/RTO, alert firing, RS256-only and per-service-key rejection. W5: release gate twice on ENVIRONMENT=production from a git-archive export of the final checkpoint tree.

Barrier order: every unit suite (one process each), then realinfra suites (at most 2 concurrent), then the wave's e2e suites, then the review package, then bug-finding rounds until one is dry (at most 3). CI mirrors the unit, contract, image build/boot and migrate layers; because nothing is pushed, 'make ci-local' is the proof until the owner commits.
risks: Clinical sign-off (D-05, D-06, D-22, D-28, D-29) may lag engineering. W1 proceeds on conservative defaults with the owner's acceptance recorded, but W5 and go-live block without a named clinician approver, and a late lexicon change re-runs the phrase suite across five detectors.

Without BAAs for Portkey/Anthropic or the SMTP relay (D-04, D-12), LLM layers stay disabled for real users and alerts cannot carry user identity. The product must remain safe and usable with templates and deterministic screening, and the pilot's value may shrink.

A recall-first lexicon can flood clinicians with false positives, and clinicians who learn to ignore pages defeat the safety path. Controls: the negative phrase set, ELEVATED-means-resources-only, per-episode coalescing, acknowledgement and monitoring of page volume.

The IF-01 bootstrap is the largest design risk: all nine services adopt it in W0, so a defect cascades everywhere. Mitigations: Opus design, AGY adversarial review before phase B, behaviour-preserving adoption, the conformance test and boot smoke in both profiles.

Running as solace_app with RLS from W0 will surface failures in flows without request context (registration, consumers, reapers, CLIs). Without acting_as_user discipline and realinfra tests, these fail silently as empty reads.

In one shared working tree, a half-finished phase-A platform edit breaks every lane's tests, and a missed handover (the user-service split files, slot files) produces silent edit conflicts. Mitigations: phase gating, the pre-dispatch disjointness check, owning-suite runs per task, full regression only at barriers and rollback.ps1 per declared paths.
Docker capacity: two concurrent full stacks (about 15 containers each) can exhaust RAM; the plan relies on at most 2 e2e lanes, Weaviate disabled by default and stack reuse within a lane.

The working tree stays uncommitted until the owner acts (D-17). One destructive git command could lose weeks of work; checkpoint trees are the only safety net, and MVP-008 cannot close without the owner's commit.

No-commit-on-failure consumer semantics risk poison-message loops and head-of-line blocking of crisis alerts; bounded in-place retries, the malformed-message DLQ path and realinfra poison tests are mandatory.

langgraph-checkpoint-postgres is not installed locally and uses psycopg rather than asyncpg; its pinned DDL (including CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) must be applied through slot 017 correctly, or checkpoint durability (MVP-066) slips. D-20 approval is a W0 entry dependency.

W2 is the largest wave (about 90 issues across 12 workstreams), and the 6-implementer cap makes it the long pole; low/medium domain items are already deferred to W5, and further slips need explicit owner acceptance.
AWS deployer permissions are blocked (D-25), so the release gate may be provable only on the local strict profile, leaving TLS/ACME, DNS, host alarms and S3 backups unproven on the real host.
The mobile client currently targets Supabase and mocks (D-11); if it is not re-pointed at IF-12, the hardened backend contract goes unused in the pilot.

E2E flakiness under timing (Kafka rebalance, SMTP retries, re-page intervals) could mask real failures or block barriers; deterministic fakes, shortened configurable intervals, bounded generous waits and the twice-green release rule are the controls.
Erasure versus duty-of-care retention (D-24) is a legal question: pseudonymizing crisis episodes and escalation records may conflict with counsel's view in either direction.

Two refusals still skip the screen (crisis-review residual): WS frames over 8 KB (WS-11.17) and REST bodies over 4000 characters (422, WS-11.4). A long crisis message gets no resources and no page. This is raised for the D-22 sign-off: either accept it, or screen the first 4000 characters before refusing.

From W2, the WS-11.7 thread-ownership lookup sits on the chat path, so a Postgres outage refuses the turn before the screen runs. WS-10's crisis path is designed to stay live during a database outage (the in-band resources need no database). Executors should keep the lookup after the screen, or fail open to the local screen, and the W2 Postgres-outage E2E (WS-05.8) must cover it.

No commits (D-17) leaves the working tree as the only full copy, and checkpoint trees are unreferenced git objects that git gc can prune after about two weeks. Mitigation: each barrier tree is exported with git archive to a zip outside the repo and copied off the machine by the owner. The owner may also approve git config gc.pruneExpire never for the program's duration (OPEN-ITEMS X-11). Never run git clean, reset or checkout in this tree.

AWS provisioning is blocked: the existing user MedCodex-Local can only call Bedrock (IAM simulation of 2026-10-19). If the deployer policy is not attached before W4, the off-host backup target is unproven; if not attached by W5 entry, the release gate stops (D-25). The owner action is X-01.

The venv baseline may differ from the 5,377 anaconda baseline (shadowed or upgraded packages, PyJWT >= 2.13). W0 entry records the per-suite venv baseline, and any drop needs a ledger Ruling before tasks start (D-20).

Bedrock model availability and quotas for the chosen Anthropic model in us-east-1 are unverified. BEDROCK_MODEL_ID is set at deploy after checking ListFoundationModels and inference profiles, and LLM features stay off for real users until the AWS BAA is recorded (D-04, X-02, X-08).

Multi-country (D-29): users from a country without verified resources would get only the generic fallback. Mitigation: pilot admission stays a named cohort (D-31), and each new locale needs clinician-verified resources before its users join (X-09).
